params.body:
## What broke

On staging, the Car-Pass chip in the own-stock list did not read "Car-Pass aanvragen". It read its own source code:

```
{ if (r === 'confirmed') { this.run('confirmCarpassChassis'); } else if (r === 'denied') { this.unknownEdit(d); } }); }, /* Annuleren in stap 2 brengt de dealer terug naar de vraag ...
```

## Why the parser did that

The chip carried sixty lines of Alpine in the value of a double-quoted `x-data` attribute, and the JavaScript comments inside that value contained double quotes of their own:

```
/* ... Stap 2 verschijnt pas na "Nummer aanpassen" en heeft nog één hoofdknop. ... */
/* ... "aanpassen" is een omweg van die ene vraag ... Stap 1 heeft "Nee". */
```

An HTML parser does not read JavaScript. It ends a double-quoted attribute at the next double quote, wherever that quote sits: in a string, in a comment, anywhere. So `x-data` stopped at `na "`, the word `Nummer` became a bare attribute, `aanpassen` became another, and the rest of the sixty lines ended up as markup and as text content inside the button. That text is what the dealer saw.

Four quoted Dutch phrases were involved; the first one is the one that did the damage.

## How many other instances

**One.** This was the only occurrence in the tree.

The whole of `resources/views` (every `.blade.php`) was scanned for a double-quoted Alpine/Livewire attribute (`x-*`, `wire:*`, `@*`, `:*`) whose HTML-parsed value cannot be a complete expression: brackets that do not balance, a block comment that never closes, an odd number of single quotes. Those three signals together flag this one attribute in `ownstock/_wagen_rij.blade.php` and produce no false positives anywhere else. That is also what made the static guard below safe to ship.

## Which shape, and why

The component moved out of the attribute, to `Alpine.data('carpassChip', ...)` in `resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php`, and the attribute became `x-data="carpassChip({{ id }}, @js($cpBody))"`.

Not just escaping the quotes, for two reasons:

- **The repo already has this shape.** `slCombo`, `slComboMulti`, `slDualRange` and `slHistoRange` are all registered in one `alpine:init` block in that layout. Sixty lines of logic belong there, next to them, and not in an attribute.
- **Escaping fixes this occurrence, not the class.** Inside a `<script>` block a quote is an ordinary character, so the failure mode does not exist there at all. The attribute now holds one expression, which is what an attribute is for.

The comments moved along **unchanged**, quotes and all: they carry the reasoning behind the two-step unknown-chassis dialog (X-95), which is worth keeping.

Two details that matter for the move: `$wire[...]` became `this.$wire[...]` (inside an `Alpine.data()` object the magic is reached through `this`), and only the two things that differ per vehicle — the id and the pre-rendered confirmation body — travel as arguments. The front-end contract in CLAUDE.md is untouched: nothing was added to `resources/js/app.js`, so the bundle gains no import/export statements and `BuildContractTest` still passes.

## Which tests now catch it

**`tests/Feature/OwnStockRowMarkupTest.php` (new, targeted).** It renders `ownstock/_wagen_rij` for a vehicle in each Car-Pass state — the action button, the Car-Pass link, the pending chip, and no connection — and reads the result back with `DOMDocument`, the way a browser reads it. Two assertions per state, both general rather than tied to this attribute:

- no visible text node anywhere in the row may contain `=>`, `{`, `}`, `this.run(`, `$wire`, `ui.dialog(`, `function`, `===` or `;` (script and style contents excluded);
- no attribute name in the row may be anything other than a name, because an attribute that ends early leaves the words that followed the quote behind as bare attributes.

Plus, for the chip itself: its `textContent` is exactly `Car-Pass aanvragen`, and its `x-data` matches `carpassChip(<id>, ...)`.

Checked against the bug: with the old row restored, this test fails with `<button> shows "{ if (r === 'confirmed') ...`.

**`tests/Feature/AlpineExpressionTest.php` (new method, broad).** The static scan described above, in the spirit of `StylesheetSyntaxTest`. It does not look for quotes — Blade's `@js()` writes plenty of legitimate escaped ones — but reads each attribute value the way the parser does, up to the first unescaped double quote, and asks whether what it got can be a whole expression. It was verified to be quiet on the current tree and to fail on the old row (`_wagen_rij.blade.php:166 x-data -> brackets do not balance, a block comment is never closed`). This test file already existed for the neighbouring failure mode (a statement where Alpine expects an expression, X-83), which is where the new method belongs.

## Why three green checks missed it

The dialogs were rendered standalone and checked on screen. A component rendered in isolation is not the component on the page, and CI renders no list row at all. Recorded as finding **X-96** on rule R S3-2.1, with the coverage snapshot and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated.

## Verified

`php artisan test --filter='OwnStockList|Carpass|CarPass|StylesheetSyntax|BuildContract|SmokeTest|ViewLogic|AlpineExpression|OwnStockRowMarkup|RulesCoverage|CompiledViews'` → 1150 assertions, no failures.

Visually confirmed on the real row (rendered through the app, not a standalone page): the button contains the Car-Pass logo and the label, and nothing else.
params.title: The Car-Pass chip showed its own code
